construction_rule: paired moderator flips; surface problem held as constant as practical; principle names absent from base context

cases.principle_prime: Dependency Inversion / Open-Closed style abstraction guidance
cases.context: A notification system has 92 existing providers. Adding one provider requires handwritten membership edits in five separate runtime/UI registries. Two independent provider-addition demands occurred within months. Provider behavior already shares one stable send contract.

action_map.ACTION_A: Introduce one backend and one frontend membership registry while keeping provider implementations/forms separate.
action_map.ACTION_B: Keep adding every provider through the existing five handwritten membership sites.
action_map.ABSTAIN: Do not prefer either structure from current evidence.

cases.principle_prime: Dependency Inversion / Open-Closed style abstraction guidance
cases.context: A platform adds integrations as self-contained component directories, each with a local manifest. Central runtime discovery is generated automatically from those manifests. New integrations do not require repeated handwritten edits to a central runtime registry.

action_map.ACTION_A: Add another handwritten central integration registry to further centralize membership.
action_map.ACTION_B: Remove the local manifests and replace them with runtime convention scanning as a different central membership mechanism.
action_map.ABSTAIN: Keep the existing local manifest/generated-discovery boundary unchanged; no new membership intervention is warranted.

cases.context: A reusable provider boundary exposes search and fetch/extract capabilities. Two successive real maintenance demands require search only. Implementers must nevertheless provide truthful conformance for fetch/extract.

action_map.ACTION_A: Split the boundary so search-only providers implement only search.
action_map.ACTION_B: Keep one wide search+fetch boundary for all providers.
action_map.ABSTAIN: Do not prefer either structure from current evidence.

cases.context: A provider boundary exposes save, load, stat, list, remove and delete. Every admitted provider demand requires all six operations and the lifecycle tests exercise all six.

action_map.ACTION_A: Split the interface into smaller capability interfaces anyway.
action_map.ACTION_B: Replace the typed six-operation backend interface with one generic execute(operation, payload) dispatcher.
action_map.ABSTAIN: Keep the current cohesive six-operation backend interface unchanged; no capability restructuring is warranted.

cases.context: Three interchangeable external implementations change independently and frequently. Client policy semantics have remained stable across those changes, and future implementation substitution is already scheduled.

action_map.ACTION_A: Bind clients to a stable policy boundary and adapt changing implementations behind it.
action_map.ACTION_B: Bind clients directly to each concrete implementation.
action_map.ABSTAIN: Do not prefer inversion or direct binding.

cases.context: A single implementation and its client semantics are changing together during a short experimental phase. Each interface revision tracks the same underlying product hypothesis, and there is no observed or scheduled implementation substitution.

action_map.ACTION_A: Introduce a stable abstraction now and force both sides through it.
action_map.ACTION_B: Keep direct binding until the semantics stabilize or substitution demand appears.

cases.context: One class owns billing-rule calculation and customer-notification formatting. Over twelve maintenance events, changes to the two concerns came from different stakeholders and never co-occurred; edits to one concern repeatedly touched tests unrelated to the other.

action_map.ACTION_A: Separate the two responsibilities behind explicit collaboration.
action_map.ACTION_B: Keep both responsibilities in one class.

cases.context: One component validates and persists a financial record. Across twelve maintenance events, validation and persistence rules changed together every time because they share one transactional invariant; splitting previous prototypes duplicated rollback logic and caused inconsistent states.

action_map.ACTION_A: Split validation and persistence into separate services solely to give each one responsibility.
action_map.ACTION_B: Keep the invariant-owning operations together while isolating unrelated concerns elsewhere.

cases.context: A parser core has received six independent format additions. The core parsing contract has remained stable; each new format varies only in decoding rules and more formats are already requested.

action_map.ACTION_A: Create an extension point for format-specific decoders while preserving the stable core contract.
action_map.ACTION_B: Continue editing the core conditional chain for every new format.

cases.context: A small internal tool has one exceptional export format required for a migration that ends next week. The format changes core semantics rather than only extension behavior, no second variant is expected, and an extension framework would outlive the tool.

action_map.ACTION_A: Build a general extension framework so the core never changes for formats.
action_map.ACTION_B: Implement the one migration-specific core change directly and remove it with the migration path.

cases.context: Three client groups use disjoint subsets of a twelve-method interface. In the last ten releases, changes to one subset forced unrelated clients to update mocks and conformance tests despite never calling those methods.

action_map.ACTION_A: Expose smaller client-specific capability interfaces backed by the same implementation.

cases.context: All three client groups call all twelve methods of an interface in each complete workflow. The methods share one lifecycle invariant, and no client-specific subset has remained stable across releases.

action_map.ACTION_A: Split the interface into smaller interfaces anyway.
action_map.ACTION_B: Broaden the interface by merging in unrelated administration and diagnostics operations.
action_map.ABSTAIN: Keep the current cohesive twelve-method interface unchanged; no interface restructuring is warranted.

reconstitution_note: v2 removes action aliasing in ABSTAIN cells only; moderators, paired families, principle primes, cell labels, precommitted choices, arms, models and scoring thresholds remain frozen.
